meta.what: Curated product policy — the single source of truth for what we promote (KEEP), what we never link (DENY), and which high-commission bets are judged as their own cohort (bet:true). Loaded by checks.mjs and re-exported as KEEP_ASINS / KEEP_BETS / DENY_ASINS.
meta.how_to_edit: Operator edits directly, or merges the bi-weekly product-audit proposal PR (product-audit.mjs --propose). Merge = approval. Entries carry topic + note so every line explains itself in a diff.
meta.chosen: 2026-07-17 from the full Levanta catalog browse + our OWN 90-day realized sales (browse-catalog.mjs). One or two proven singles per topic, ranked by realized $/conversions, then commission, then platform EPC.
meta.allow_note: MERGED MENU (operator 2026-08-23: 'expand the allowlist — maybe it should merge so we don't have to manually update like this all the time'). The engine's selection menu is now KEEP ∪ allow (checks.mjs ALLOW_ASINS): one curated list, and the bi-weekly product-audit maintains it — merging its proposal PR adds the proven and drops the dead with no second hand-edit. `allow` remains only as a slot for temporary extras not yet promoted into keep; the exploration off-switch is PRODUCT_ALLOWLIST=0, no longer emptying this array. History: the sprint allowlist (2026-08-15, 8 -> 14 -> 18) existed because conversion is anti-viral and product IS the conversion rate (proven brands 5-7% CVR vs house brands 0.2-0.7%; August sent 66% of clicks to sub-1.5%-CVR products) — that protection now lives in the audit pruning keep plus the realized-EPC ranking, proven-loser floor and 0.2x catalog-EPC haircut in pick-product. NO ACCOUNT LANES (operator 2026-08-16): a product is chosen by the THREAD, never by which account is writing it; pickFallback draws from this merged menu fleet-wide. DEDUPED 2026-08-25: 8 products were listed in BOTH keep and allow, so the bi-weekly audit wrote to two entries and their notes drifted apart. `allow` now holds only products NOT in keep; the selection menu (ALLOW_ASINS) is unchanged because it was always the union.

meta.floor_2026_09_19:
RAISED THE FLOOR + STOCK-CHECKED THE SHELF (operator 2026-09-19: "remove losing low performing products -- must check for instock before we start plugging. If EPC is below bar, then remove them" / "raise the floor of performance to epc 0.45").
  THE FLOOR does the removing, and it lives in laws.product.minEpcFloor, not in this file. pick-product's provenLoser now refuses any product judged at 100+ clicks whose RESTATED EPC (rate-moves.mjs) is under $0.45, which on the 2026-09-19 board is 14 of the entries still listed below. They stay on the menu deliberately: candidates() only applies the floor WHILE a converter remains in the topic, so a lane is never starved into shipping with no plug at all, and the moment a product's rate or performance recovers it is eligible again with no edit here. Judging on the restated EPC is what saved B0DZ33GTQ2, whose measured $0.260 fails the floor and whose restated $0.610 clears it after Sports Research took us 15% -> 40% on 2026-09-11.
  TAKING THEM OFF THE MENU as well is a bigger change than it looks and is NOT done here: 11 of 26 account defaults and 6 BRIDGE routes point at those 14 ASINs, and 4 of those accounts (bloodsugar, gut, testosterone) have no surviving product in their topic to be re-pointed at. That is an operator decision about what those pages sell, not a mechanical substitution.
  REMOVED HERE are only the 4 that cannot ship at all: every Formulation Factory SKU came back 'not found in the accessible catalog' on a live lookup, and none holds a products.json row, so the weekly product-health stock sync never saw them and mint would 404. B0DK61GRD2 is the one this caught that nothing else would have -- restated EPC $0.536, comfortably ABOVE the new floor, and unshippable; an EPC bar alone would have promoted it into the run. Kept in `retired` with the reason so a restored partnership is a one-line move back. Nothing reads `retired`; it is a record.
meta.floorExempt_2026_09_19:
floorExempt — the operator's override on the $0.45 absolute floor, per product.
  pick-product's provenLoser skips an entry carrying it, so the product stays pickable however far under the floor it sits. It is deliberately NOT a topic-level or lane-level switch: the floor exists to stop us plugging what does not earn, and the only safe way to weaken it is one named product at a time, each carrying the operator's own words for why.
  It does NOT override DENY, and it does not override stock -- an exempt product that is out of the catalog or sold out is still unbuyable and still skipped, because the reason there is a dead link rather than a weak one.
  Review these whenever the floor moves. An exemption that outlives its reason is how the old flat $0.03 floor stopped meaning anything.
